newsitem.title: USA: Con Ed proposes rate freeze, restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Con Ed proposes rate freeze, restructuring.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc said it has proposed a five-year rate freeze and a new corporate structure in a filing with New York regulators.
The plan filed with the New York State Public Service Commission calls for establishment of wholesale competition in the state by the middle of next year, spokesman Richard D. Mulleri said.

Although the commission had called for wholesale competition in January, creation of the ISO -- independent system operator -- to handle transmission of the power purchased and sold has fallen behind that schedule.

Asked about New York State Electric and Gas Corp's proposal to start wholesale competition August 1, 1997, Spokeswoman Katherine Karlson said the utility sees "no fully functional ISO before mid-1997."
Con Edison said it proposed a corporate structure that initially would consist of a holding company with four subsidiaries -- one regulated and three unregulated.
It said the regulated subsidiary would provide transmission and distribution of electricity.
A second subsidiary would be an energy service company which would buy power from generators and sell it to users.
The other subsidiaries would be an energy supply company and a new ventures company.
The energy supply company would own and operate electric generation, which might include some Con Edison units, the company said.
Mulleri said other Con Ed plants might be closed or sold.
The company said the new ventures company initially would invest in energy infrastructure development projects as well as market technical services.
Con Edison said its proposed electric rate plan freezes rates for five years beginning in April 1997.
It said the plan provides for accelerated depreciation of stranded investments and recovery of above-market costs under contracts for power with non-utility generators.
The utility said it also proposed a new economic development rate designed to encourage industrial customers to locate in New York or expand their existing facilities in the company's service area.
It said rates under the Manufacturers' Expansion Program would be 25 to 30 percent below standard rates.
In addition, the company said, it proposed continuing its existing Business Incentive Rate.

Under Con Edison's retail competition plan, a group of customers would be given the option to choose alternative electricity providers in 1998. The initial phase would involve some 5,600 customers with a total peak demand of 100 megawatts.
It is expected all customers desiring to choose an alternative energy supplier would have the opportunity to do so by 2003, it added.
